text:
Sasha: Quick follow-up to the prefix cache conversation. Proposal: split the notions of 'ownership' (who has the canonical right to accept writes) and 'residency' (which node currently stores the KV bytes) to reduce synchronous handoff costs and eviction blocking. Draft details: ownership token carries an epoch + fence, residency has a separate residency_epoch and soft_demote flag.

Maria: Sounds promising. Biggest concern is preserving read-after-write semantics during async handoffs. How do we avoid serving stale reads or dropping writes?

Sasha: Plan is: 1) Writes are tagged with ownership_fence; if a write hits a node with older fence it either forwards to current owner or returns a retryable error. 2) Residency transitions are asynchronous; the new owner will only start serving writes after it has residency_epoch >= ownership_epoch and has fetched necessary prefixes. 3) A short forwarding window lets the previous resident forward recent writes to the new owner to avoid data loss.

Ajay: Forwarding window implies potential double-apply. How do we prevent duplicates?

Sasha: Storage layer must be idempotent via op_ids. We also reject applies from lower-fence owners. If both nodes briefly accept, dedupe at apply-time prevents divergence. We'll add a small debug metric for duplicate-op hits.

Chen: Eviction oscillation is my worry. If residency flips rapidly we could thrash hot keys and waste bandwidth. Any smoothing?

Sasha: Introduce soft_demote + grace_ms on residency records. Evict marks soft_demote=true and starts a grace timer. During grace, reads still serve but trigger prefetch heuristics; frequent reads accelerate handoff instead of repeated eviction/re-residency cycles. Also rate-limit forced migrations per-prefix.

Maria: Can you show a lightweight proto sketch for tokens so infra can wire telemetry?

Sasha: Sure (compact):
OwnershipToken(prefix, owner_node, owner_epoch, fencing_nonce, tags)
ResidencyRecord(prefix, resident_node, residency_epoch, soft_demote, grace_ms)

Ajay: Rollout strategy? We need feature flag and telemetry for safety.

Sasha: Feature flag ownership_decouple. Canary plan: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%. Telemetry: forwarded_write_rate, forward_rpc_p95/p99, duplicate_apply_count, eviction_churn_per_prefix, prefetch_rate, read/write tail latencies (p99/p999), error/retry rates. Add chaos: simulate split/merge and long replay logs.

Chen: Integration tests we should add: 1) write during handoff -> ensure RAWR with either forward or retry, 2) twin-writes at both nodes -> idempotency/dedupe validation, 3) soft_demote grace behavior under hot read bursts, 4) prefix split that moves half the keys mid-handoff.

Maria: I'll own the eviction/handoff chaos harness and add deterministic RAWR scenarios. Ajay can take split/merge + replay determinism.

Ajay: ACK. I'll add smoke tests that assert no lost writes under forwarding and a metric that counts forwarded-but-succeeded vs forwarded-and-retried.

infra-bot: ci/ownership_decouple: unit 298 tests passed, integration 12/12. :white_check_mark:

Sasha: Thanks. I'll open the rollout PR with the flag, telemetry hooks, and a brief operator playbook (how to revert, how to force-residency). Will link PR back to the RFC doc.
